text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated paging + NCCL stall signals on kv-cache TP shards in eu-west-1. P1 triggered. Auto-page to #incidents and oncall. Summary: increased continuous-batching throughput -> unexpected cache growth -> paging -> NCCL rendezvous timeouts on TP groups.

maria oncall: seeing it. tail latency climbing, some worker OOMs and 503s. Dumping quick metrics now.

raj runtime: can confirm NCCL timeouts around 15:42 UTC, happened across 3 TP groups (grp-7, grp-12, grp-19). pattern: big prefixes -> persistent KV cache expansion -> heavy paging into CPU -> NcclRun sync stalls.

anya ml: initial guess: continuous-batching config we rolled yesterday (batch_rate=adaptive, max_seq=4096) let certain long-history customers generate giant KV entries; combined with new shard map it created skew.

maria oncall: customer impact? which customers affected?

jules support: AcmeHealth and BrightCart reported 5-25s latency spikes and intermittent 503s. We're receiving support tickets referencing model timeouts.

sam pager: @maria please escalate to SRE playbook "kv-cache-paging" and follow hotfix path. I'll coordinate comms.

maria oncall: running quick mitigation checklist: 1) disable continuous batching globally for affected pool, 2) set kv_cache.max_entries=6e6 per-shard, 3) increase paging threshold to 80% mem, 4) restart tp-daemons gracefully in blue pool. Executing step 1 now.

ops-bot: command executed: /runtime-config set continuous_batching=false --scope=eu-west-1-pool-3 --requester=maria

raj runtime: I pushed a live patch to runtime to short-circuit new batching hook (hotfix id: tp_batch_hotfix_2026_03_15). Will roll to canary 10% now.

anya ml: also pushing a mapping check to detect uneven kv_shard assignments. small script:

```
# shard imbalance check (quick)
python scripts/check_shard_balance.py --pool eu-west-1-pool-3 --threshold 1.5
```

maria oncall: initial telemetry after disabling continuous batching: tail p95 dropped from ~4.2s to ~600ms in 7 mins. Paging rate reduced by ~78%. NCCL timeouts stopped showing for grp-12 and grp-19. grp-7 still has intermittent ~1-2s stalls.

raj runtime: grp-7 had a stale shard mapping: two TP workers had overlapping kv ranges leading to hot partition. I'm going to force a resync of the shard map on grp-7 nodes and drain then restart the tp-daemon on each GPU. Will do rolling restart to avoid full pool outage.

maria oncall: approve. Prioritize nodes with highest page rates.

jules support: sending customer update: "We've applied a mitigation and are seeing improvement. Some customers may still see brief elevated latencies; please reach out if you hit errors."

sam pager: tagging sales/CS for affected accounts: @jules, please coordinate proactive outreach to AcmeHealth/SalesEng contact.

ops-bot: planned action log:
- 15:48 UTC disable continuous-batching (done)
- 15:51 UTC set kv_cache.max_entries=6000000 (in progress)
- 15:54 UTC shard-resync grp-7 (in progress)
- 16:02 UTC rolling tp-daemon restarts on affected nodes

maria oncall: note: applied cache cap per-shard to limit runaway growth. If we see increased token cost we may revert later, but customer experience priority now.

raj runtime: doing rolling restarts with this command:

```
for n in $(cat affected_nodes.txt); do
  ssh $n 'systemctl restart tp-daemon' && sleep 20
done
```

maria oncall: logs from one of the heavier nodes (sanitized):

```
[15:37:12] kv_cache: insert_size=12MB total_entries=12.1M used=8.9GB paging_rate=317/s
[15:37:18] nccl: rendezvous_timeout gid=grp-7 tid=0 duration=18.3s
[15:38:04] oom_killer invoked python3 pid=4421 (tp-daemon)
```

anya ml: root cause hypothesis to capture later: batching config + long-prefix workloads -> extremely large KV entries -> single-shard hotness due to unlucky token range assignment after recent map change -> paging thrash -> NCCL collective waits. We'll add a guard to limit per-request kv-insert size.

maria oncall: current status: p95 per-pool back to ~700ms, NCCL timeouts cleared on all but one node which finished restart at 16:01. No new OOMs since restarts. Customer 503s stopped.

sam pager: marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep oncall watch for 2 hours then transition to postmortem. @anya @raj please own next steps: a) rollback or adjust continuous-batching config b) implement per-request kv size guard c) permanent shard-balance fix + monitoring.

raj runtime: already drafted the patch to enforce per-shard max-entry-size and added a flag to runtime to reject inserts > 4MB. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5421. I'll fast-track review.

anya ml: will add an eval to our stability suite to simulate long-prefix bursts with disabled batching and with size guard. Also will add tests for shard imbalance scenarios.

maria oncall: handoff: I'm paged off at 17:30 UTC. @sam pager will be primary after that. Leaving watch until 17:45. Please post a short incident summary when fully stable.

jules support: CS note: sent proactive emails to primary contacts at AcmeHealth and BrightCart. No escalations so far.

ops-bot: incident-bot update: severity downgraded to P2 at 16:10 UTC — mitigations applied and customer impact addressed.

sam pager: thanks team. Immediate action items captured. Postmortem owners: eng-runtime (raj) and eng-ml (anya). We'll schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

maria oncall: final: recommend we add a runtime guard that prevents continuous-batching from creating KV entries above N bytes and add an automated shard-balancer that triggers before heavy loads. I'll file infra tickets. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-KV-PAGING assigned id INC-20260315-0912. Please attach logs and links to the postmortem doc.

raj runtime: linking patch and runbook in the incident doc.

anya ml: agreed. will prepare regression tests.

jules support: closing the customer-facing loop after 24h of stability.

maria oncall: thanks everyone. I'm offwatch. leaving a short runbook note under the incident doc with exact commands used for rollback and mitigation.

sam pager: copy — will do a final check in 2 hours and then close this channel for the incident.

incident-bot: This thread is now archived under incidents/INC-20260315-0912 once closed."
